title: A Taste of REST and fetch
summary: A first peek at loading data from the internet. We'll go deeper later.
heading: A Taste of REST and fetch

blocks.text: Most apps don't keep all their data inside themselves — they ask a server for it. A REST API is just a set of web addresses you can call to get or send data. Your code makes a request, the server sends a response back.

blocks.alt: Illustrated overview of REST APIs and fetch
blocks.caption: REST and fetch at a glance
Your app asks; the server answers.

blocks.text: This is a quick taste only — we'll cover REST properly in a later chapter.
fetch is the built-in way to call an API. It returns the response a moment later, so we use .then(...) to handle the data once it arrives. Press Run to load a real item from a free practice API.

items: A REST API is a set of web addresses for getting and sending data.
Your app makes a request; the server sends a response.
fetch calls an API, and .then(...) handles the data when it arrives.
